rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Re-derived fresh (shape_hash changed since the last stamped pass) -- re-walked every pronoun/demonstrative/definite-noun across all 9 chunks. Closest calls: (a) chunk 0 L7 'Come to Module 1 with the repo picked, the curated skills installed, and one trivial bug' uses definite articles with no textual antecedent at the very first chunk -- stays inside as a generic preview construction ('bring your ID'-shaped), not a specific-system reference; each item is elaborated by its own later chunk (repo: chunk 2, skills: chunk 5, bug: chunks 1/6), and chunk-0 lede nouns reused later are exactly the carve-out's own example shape. (b) chunk 6 L62 'push back if it dumps all four criteria at once' names 'four criteria' two lines before the fenced prompt (L64-) that enumerates them -- forward-pointing but inside the SAME chunk/slide, so a reader sees the full criteria list on the same projected slide; parallels rule 12's explicit same-chunk carve-out ('the prompt below... spatially true'). (c) chunk 1 L22 'the curated security skills install when you extract the bundle' -- 'the bundle' has no in-body antecedent yet at that point (the tarball is first named L45, 'the bundle' as a term first appears in chunk 5's own header L51) -- stays inside for the same preview-construction reason as (a), and the sentence's teaching point (skills auto-install at extraction) doesn't hinge on resolving 'the bundle' at that moment. All other definite references resolve sequentially: chunk 3 L40 'the repo you just picked' -> chunk 2; chunk 6 L66 'the candidate-bug screen' -> chunk 6 L60/62 (in-chunk); chunk 8 L80 'The bug you picked' -> chunk 6.

Two off-file links in the body, both named not located: chunk 2 L34 '[build one from zero](trainings/agentic-engineering-101/supplementary/build-a-project-from-zero.md)' names the destination in the link text itself; chunk 7 L76 'Simon Willison, [Vibe engineering](...)' names author and title in the same sentence. Ran `node scripts/check-slide-deixis.js --file curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/prework.md --links` this session -- both links listed, named not located. No 'the opening lecture said' style positional callback anywhere in the body.

The only backward-pointing phrasing, chunk 8 L80 'The bug you picked', resolves within this same file (chunk 6), which is rule 1's domain, not a cross-beat module reference.

rules_evaluated.evidence: Grepped body for 'guess'/'predict'/'take a guess' -- zero hits. No guess-before-reveal construction anywhere; prework has no live-demo beat to break.

Ran `node scripts/check-slide-size.js --report --file curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/prework.md` this session -- thinnest chunk '3. Get the content folder onto your laptop' still carries two self-standing instructions (fetch-tarball prompt; manual-download fallback link), not a bare wait-state bullet. All 8 `##` chunks carry a self-carrying claim; no orphan found.

Checked all 8 headers against their own chunk content, with particular attention to chunk 6 ('5. Pick a trivial bug and confirm Module 1 readiness') since its lead paragraph was shortened under this pin: new L60 'Ask Claude to screen three trivial bug candidates and confirm the repo is ready for Module 1' restates both header halves (pick-a-bug / confirm-readiness) directly -- header still self-carries, no drift from the edit. Closest-to-violating elsewhere: chunk 4 '3. Get the content folder onto your laptop' (L43) -- its content (L45) only asks the student to fetch the .tar.gz archive, which becomes an actual folder only after chunk 5's extraction step. Stays inside: nothing in the chunk contradicts the header, chunk 5's own header 'Extract the bundle' makes the two-step split explicit, and 'folder' names the well-understood eventual outcome rather than a false claim about this slide alone. Every other header matches its content exactly.

Checked all 5 sub-items across all 9 chunks. Ran `grep -n -E "Not [A-Z][a-z]+\. Not " curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/prework.md` this session -> 0 hits. No anaphora/epistrophe triple anywhere. No self-grading superlative (the blocking sub-item) -- grepped for 'one of the most'/'the best'/'the most useful' -- zero hits. No number-plus-own-retraction: L18 'Roughly 30 to 120 minutes of the agent working' is a plain labelled estimate, not a number stated then undercut; the runtime-minutes breakdown sits in the maintainer block, out of body scope. No abstraction-noun stack -- vocabulary stays concrete (repo, tarball, skills, bug, PR) throughout. No empty-leg verb triplet -- the readiness prompt's 'test, branch, commit, and open a PR' names four distinct concrete actions, none vacuous.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Ran `grep -n -iE "compendium|forcing function|\bbeat\b|\bmood\b|firing|Connections" curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/prework.md` this session -- only hits sit below the maintainer cut (L84), zero in-body. Ran `grep -n -i surface` -- two body hits, L17 'user-facing surface' and L29 'surface area for rules and memory to land on' -- both the ordinary attack-surface/API-surface engineering family, not the repo's writing-surface-as-noun jargon the rule carves out. 'Plan mode' (L16) is a real Claude Code product feature, not curriculum-internal dialect; this training teaches it directly. '**Session**' (L38) is the architecture-mandated widget label, not narrative dialect. Expanded prompt-block text (chunks 4-6, via `node scripts/expand-md.js`) is plain engineering vocabulary throughout -- no dialect terms found there either.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget -- bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Grepped `\*\*` over the raw body. Chunk 1 L15-18 carry one short (<=4-word) bold handle per bullet ('Trivial bug', 'A small multi-file task', 'A small feature', 'A bigger piece') labelling four task-size checklist entries a reader scans to find their own size -- the reading-list/menu waiver applies by function (a task-size inventory meant to be scanned for an entry point, not read straight through), each bold is well under the <=5-word handle cap, and no whole-sentence bold appears anywhere in the section (the rule's actual violation shape). Confirmed no sibling 'Bring to Module N' section in this training uses the same 4-bullet-bold-handle shape: earn-the-trust.md's 'Bring to Module 4' instead uses one whole bolded sentence under the sanctioned section 34 floor-ceiling exception; learn-from-the-test.md's and run-the-first-experiment.md's Bring sections carry no bold at all. Prework's own maintainer block already rules the section 34 callout N/A here ('no bolded not-an-epic line is owed on this page'), so the bold present is judged solely on the menu-waiver, not on section 34. Chunk 3 '**Session**' and chunks 4-6 '**Prompt** *(Claude Code)*' are architecture-mandated widget chrome -- confirmed raw source L47/55/64/68 are bare `{{prompt:}}` markers, not literal bold in source -- so they carry no authored bold to budget against. Chunk 7 L76 carries exactly one bolded element, '**Read:**' (1 word, title left plain) -- the literal sanctioned reading-list shape. No chunk exceeds budget.

Ran `node scripts/check-slide-size.js --report --file curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/prework.md` this session, which iterates the composed-deck model and returned exactly those 8 chunk headings with word/bullet counts -- no chunk silently absent. `grep -n "prework" scripts/build-workbook.js` shows prework pushed into the same `allModules` array every ordered module goes through, wrapped in `<section class="module" id=...>` -- the wrapper `buildDeckModel` (site/layouts/slides.js) walks to reach the composed deck. The 2026-07-09 failure mode the rule warns about (prework silently dropped from the deck) does not reproduce here.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: All 8 body headings are imperative/phase-label style ('Bring real work', '1. Pick THE repo' ... '5. Pick a trivial bug and confirm Module 1 readiness', 'Bring to Module 1') matching the exercise-heading convention -- prework is a task walkthrough, not a lecture, so the declarative-claim requirement doesn't bind. No slide here is a law/consolidation moment where the header IS the teaching. 'Pre-read before Module 1' and 'Bring to Module 1' read as the rule's own orientation/catalogue-label carve-out, not mislabelled claims.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies -- three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Checked all three classes against every bullet/sentence in all 9 chunks. (a) doctrine restatement -- none found; prework is pure M0 logistics with no prior lens/split/law to re-announce, and the 4 task-size bullets (chunk 1) and 3 repo-criteria bullets (chunk 2) each add a distinct move/object. (b) self-referential design commentary -- none; no sentence tells the student they are inside a pedagogy or names the curriculum's own design intent. (c) aphorism kicker -- closest candidate chunk 6 L70 'Small steer, small trick. A minute here, another there.' -- stays inside: it is concrete to the specific AskUserQuestion tip just given (L66-68), ties together both the push-back move and the fallback trick just described, and is not a restatement of the header or a `**The point:**`-style line. `grep -rn 'small steer\|small trick' curriculum/` confirms this phrasing is not a coined term restated from elsewhere in the corpus (self-hits only). No bullet meeting the 'carries nothing' bar found.
